knowledge_type_note: Motif (D). Its relationship to the strategic principle of two weaknesses is a genuine structural link, not an analogy of convenience.
definition_short: A piece with two defensive jobs cannot do both; take one and the other collapses.
definition_long:
A single unit is the only defender of two things. The tactic exploits the fact that answering one threat abandons the other. It is listed as a category in the Encyclopedia of Chess Middlegames.

Overloading is the tactical form of the same logic that the PRINCIPLE OF TWO WEAKNESSES applies strategically: finite defensive resources stretched across more duties than they can cover. The difference is timescale — overloading resolves in a move or two, two weaknesses over dozens.

history.notes: Tactical motifs are descriptive pattern names of long and mostly anonymous usage. The Chess Informant classification is cited as a standard enumeration, not as the origin of the term.

preconditions: One enemy unit is the sole defender of two distinct targets or duties
indicators_for: Removing or diverting that unit leaves both targets loose
The two duties require the piece to be on different squares
indicators_against: A second defender covers one of the duties
The piece can perform both duties from one square
Capturing the overloaded piece is answered by a recapture that restores the defence

exceptions: A defender that appears overloaded may be adequate if one 'duty' was never real.
limitations: Depends on enumerating duties, which is a functional judgement.

examples.note: Constructed. The rook on d8 has two jobs: it defends the knight on d5 down the file, and it is the only guard of the back rank. Rxd5 asks it to do both at once - if it recaptures it leaves e8, and Re8 is mate. The engine's own line is the demonstration: after Rxd5 it plays ...Rb8 rather than ...Rxd5, which is to say Black DECLINES the recapture and simply loses a knight. That is what overloading means, and it is why this base refuses to detect the motif mechanically: the geometry here is a rook on a file, and what makes it overloading is a mate on a different file that has not happened yet.

engine.verdict_note: +6.73 at depth 22, settled at depth 14, and the engine plays Rxd5. The size is the evidence: a knight plus the refused recapture, in a position where material was level before the move.

counterexamples.note: Registered false-positive case `two-defenders-for-two-duties`, kept on the record as well as in tests/false_positive_cases.json so that the concept carries its own negative evidence. THE SURFACE PATTERN IS PRESENT: A black rook on d8 defends the knight on d5 down the file, the black king is boxed in on the back rank, and White has rooks on d1 and e1. Every piece of the overloading picture is on the board, and it is this record's positive example with one man added. WHY IT IS NOT THE CONCEPT: The one man added is a second black rook, on e8. Overloading is a claim that ONE piece is asked to do two jobs at once; here there are two pieces and two jobs. After Rxd5 Rxd5, the rook on e8 still guards the back rank and there is no mate. WHAT THE SYSTEM DOES: The API does not report overloading. Stockfish 18 says -4.30 at depth 22 and its first move is Rxe8+, trading into a position where Black is a knight up — so Rxd5, the move that works in the positive example, is simply a blunder here. Read against this record's positive at +6.73: one rook added to the defence and the same move goes from winning a knight to losing one. This record has no matcher, and the reason is on the record — an overload is a claim about being asked to do both at once, which is a property of what the attacker can arrange rather than of what is on the board.

ambiguous_examples.note: The overload configuration exactly: the rook on d8 defends the knight on d5 down the file AND is the only guard of the back rank, and White's rook is on d1 facing it. It does not work, because White has only one rook - Rxd5 is met by Rxd5 and the back-rank threat never arrives, so the black rook is asked to do one job at a time and can. The position is -0.01. Read against this record's positive example, which is the same picture with a SECOND white rook on e1: one piece added, and the rook on d8 goes from comfortable to unable to recapture. Filed as ambiguous because the configuration the concept names is fully present and the concept is not: an overload is a claim about being asked to do both at once, and nobody is asking.

engine.verdict_note: -0.01 at depth 24, settled at depth 21, and the engine's move is a quiet pawn push - it does not try Rxd5 at all. The positive example on this record, one rook further, is +6.73.

by_level.beginner: That piece is guarding two things at once. Take one and it cannot keep guarding the other.
by_level.intermediate: The {piece} is overloaded — it is the only defender of both {a} and {b}.
by_level.advanced: Overloading. The tactical counterpart of the principle of two weaknesses: the same finite-defence logic on a shorter timescale.
